comment: The factory obligations register (0.9.0) — every forward-looking debt this release carries, in ONE machine-read home, read by scripts/check-obligations.mjs (clockless in lint.yml's machinery block; --clockful ONLY in hygiene.yml's scheduled job). The release's obligations previously lived in three unjoined sources — the ramp fleet (rampNote sites + template/migrations.json records), template/base/tools/deferrals.json, and prose — and gates-catalog.md's docs-sync section recorded the factory-side reader debt this register discharges.

Row schema: { id, kind: release|calendar|condition, target (x.y.z for release; YYYY-MM-DD for calendar; null for condition), sites?: [{file, mustContain?}] (prose anchors, ONE-WAY — the register is the index, the sites are anchors; the both-ways closure is the consumer scan's grammar and was the vacuous-port trap factory-side), reason (>= 40 chars), reviewedOn (YYYY-MM-DD), evidence (URL or repo file ref — REQUIRED for kind:condition) }.

Kinds: release reds CLOCKLESSLY when package.json reaches the target (check-ramp-ledger.mjs's version authority); calendar is judged ONLY under --clockful in the scheduled lane (a verdict that changes with the date must never red a PR); condition NEVER reds on time — shape + evidence is its bar, and discharging one is DELETING it in a reviewed diff.

Unions the reader closes: every template/base/tools/deferrals.json entry id has a condition-or-release row here under the same id (the census); every shipped rampNote site whose `until` is still in the future has a kind:release row targeting its expiry version (the debt the next migrations record will owe, written down before it is due).

DELIBERATELY NOT LEDGERED: .harness/pending/source-fixes.json — it is CONSUMER-side, parked by `update` on the install and self-clearing via the probes in template/migrations.json seededSourceFixes (owned there, checked by scripts/check-seeded-migrations.mjs); a factory row would be a second, staler copy of a record that already has an owner.

obligations.reason: ASD opened consultation on 2026-06-15 to replace the Essential Eight with an ISM-grounded 'Essentials' series (Essentials for enterprise IT first), citing the cloud gap explicitly; reported at roughly 12 months to deprecation and 24 to retirement. Everything built against the E8 in 0.9.9 therefore has a bounded shelf life, and the stated reason for the change IS the product-versus-organisation mismatch tools/essential-eight.json documents. Judged in the scheduled lane only: a verdict that changes with the date must never red a PR. On arrival, re-verify against ASD and either re-date this row or retarget the register at the successor framework.

Essential Eight MFA-11, MFA-12 and MFA-14 require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication at ML3, and the platform cannot supply it today. TOTP is not phishing-resistant. Supabase WebAuthn MFA does produce aal2 (GoTrue IsAAL2Claim accepts mfa/webauthn) but is undocumented, absent from the Dashboard, marked @experimental in auth-js, challengeAndVerify is TOTP-only, and it is a billable add-on the CLI silently downgrades to false when cost is not confirmed. Passkeys are a SEPARATE aal1 primary sign-in system and do not satisfy it. This is a platform ceiling, not a schedule: it discharges when WebAuthn MFA ships documented and dashboard-reachable, by deleting this row and regrading the three requirements together.

Essential Eight MFA-09 ("MFA is used to authenticate users of data repositories") is graded not-implemented for a COVERAGE reason, not an enforcement one. 0.9.9 shipped the rail — private.mfa_is_required() (SECURITY DEFINER, no grant on auth.mfa_factors) behind a RESTRICTIVE aal2 policy with no FOR clause, proven against a live stack by supabase/tests/mfa_aal2.test.sql, which reds against the vendor-published policy — but applied it to public.notes alone, the worked vertical every slice is copied from. Which data warrants a second factor is a product decision: a low-sensitivity lookup table blocked at aal1 is a support ticket, not a control. Discharge is either a reviewed per-table register with a two-way closure, or a decision (recorded here) that coverage stays the consumer’s. ADR: docs/adr/20260812-mfa-aal2.md.

Essential Eight MFA-01, MFA-04 and MFA-06 all say MFA "is used to authenticate" users or customers — a claim about ALL of them — and mandatory enrolment is NOT expressible in GoTrue: MFAConfiguration carries no Required field and there is no project-level require-MFA switch for end users. 0.9.9 shipped the enforcement half (the aal2 rail makes enrolment MEAN something: an enrolled user cannot reach the data with a password alone, on any surface) and deliberately not the enrolment surface, which needs a signup state machine and a challenge flow on both product surfaces. Until it exists, a user who never enrols authenticates with one factor and these rows stay not-implemented rather than being softened to alternate-control. Same shape as dsr-web-erase-surface: the rail exists, the surface is owed. ADR: docs/adr/20260812-mfa-aal2.md.

Essential Eight MFA-15 and MFA-16 want authentication events centrally logged and protected. 0.9.9 established what is actually there, against a running stack rather than from documentation: auth.audit_log_entries EXISTS in every Supabase project (a first draft of the register wrongly said auth events were captured nowhere), a signup and a sign-in write rows to it, and THREE failed sign-ins write nothing — so the "unsuccessful" half of MFA-15 has no record at all. It is also unprotected in a way audit.events is not: zero non-internal triggers, and `postgres` holds UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, so there is no append-only layer and none can be added without editing a schema GoTrue owns and re-migrates. Discharge is not a harness gate: it is either an application-level auth-event trail written into audit.events at the sign-in seam (which would capture the unsuccessful half the platform drops) or an operator log drain, and the second is Dashboard-only. Recorded rather than scheduled until the shape is decided.

Essential Eight RAP-20, RAP-21, AC-11, AC-12 and UAH-20 all turn on the word "centrally". The events this repository can produce ARE produced and ARE protected — audit.events is append-only in four layers and 0.9.9 added the elevated-role ATTEMPT (service_role trying to read, forge, modify, delete and truncate) rather than inferring refusal from a grant lookup, which is the difference between ASD's POOR and EXCELLENT evidence tiers. What no part of this repository can do is forward them: central logging means the record survives compromise of the system that produced it, and an in-database trail does not. THE FORWARDING HALF IS ASYMMETRIC AND MUST NOT BE GATED AS THOUGH IT WERE SYMMETRIC: one platform's log drains are API- and Terraform-addressable, the other's are Dashboard-only (verified negative against the live Management API specification — `drain` appears only as an enum value, never as a path). A gate resolving either from a live endpoint is refused outright by this repository's hermeticity rule (CONTRIBUTING: a gate that resolves its expectations from a live third-party endpoint turns an untouched commit red overnight, and this repo has already paid for that once). Retention is the other half of the reason: platform log retention tops out at 90 days by plan tier, so any requirement beyond that must ride a drain into a sink the operator controls. Discharge is a reviewed decision about WHERE the boundary sits, not a scheduled build.

Essential Eight RB-02 wants backups of data, applications AND settings synchronised to a common point in time. 0.9.9 shipped the evidence lane (`backup-evidence`, tools/check-backup-posture.mjs) and established that it does NOT discharge this row, for a reason worth recording rather than rediscovering: the platform's backup does not contain two of the three asset classes. Verified against the vendor's own pages — Edge Functions, Auth settings and API keys, Realtime settings, extensions and project settings, read replicas and Storage API objects all sit outside the database backup (the database holds only Storage metadata), and custom-role LOGIN passwords are stripped from it. The sharpest exclusion is the Vault/pgsodium root key: a backup carries ciphertext but never the key, so a restore into a NEW project cannot decrypt what it just restored until the key is carried across by hand — which is also the thing most likely to be discovered during a real recovery rather than before one. Discharge is a manifest that binds the database backup to the commit, the migration set and the deployed function versions, emitted at deploy time. Not built, and not scheduled: it needs a deploy-time artefact channel this repository does not yet have.

Essential Eight RB-03/RB-05/RB-06/RB-09 concern where backups live and who can reach them. 0.9.9 recorded what the vendor ATTESTS, labelled as attestation rather than as anything this system demonstrates: backups are AES-256 encrypted at rest with keys protected by FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs, stored in S3 on infrastructure independent of the project's own resources. That is a contractual statement in the data processing agreement, not an artefact any control here reads, so it cannot raise a grade. Two things remain unpublished and are recorded as unknowns rather than assumed either way: no storage region for backups is stated, and whether daily backups aging past the plan window (7 / 14 / 30 days) are DELETED or merely made inaccessible is never said — every statement takes the form "can access the last N days", which is an access claim and not a deletion one. RB-05/06/09 stay graded as they were, because "no client role can reach a backup" is true here only because this tree produces no backups of its own: vacuous truth, and the register's own rule is that absence of a surface is never a control. Discharge is a self-produced off-platform backup with its own store and IAM policy, which is an operator decision about where the boundary sits rather than a build to schedule.

Essential Eight RB-11 requires backup administrator accounts to be prevented from modifying and deleting backups during the retention period. 0.9.9 re-verified the platform surface and the finding got SHARPER AND WEAKER AT THE SAME TIME, which is the point. Sharper: no Delete or Modify action for a backup appears anywhere — not as a row in the published permissions table, and not as any method across all 115 API paths. Weaker: that is an ABSENCE OF SURFACE, not a published control. Supabase nowhere states that backups cannot be deleted; it simply never offers the verb, and no page publishes an immutability, WORM or object-lock guarantee for the buckets holding them (searched: the backups guide, product security, the SOC 2 and HIPAA pages, the shared-responsibility model, the PITR usage page). Reading an unoffered verb as prevention would be exactly the inflation this register exists to refuse. There is also no backup-administrator role to separate: the four published roles are Owner, Administrator, Developer and Read-Only, the table grants backups only View/Download/Restore and PITR only View/Restore, `Developer` holds Download and Restore while being described as unable to change project settings, and `Read-Only` — the only role narrow enough to resemble a custodian — is denied both and is gated behind Team or Enterprise. ONE GAP IS EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIABLE AND MUST NOT BE GRADED IN EITHER DIRECTION: whether reducing the PITR recovery retention period, or removing the PITR add-on, destroys backup data already inside the previous window. The vendor documents the billing consequence and says the period can be changed, and publishes no data-lifecycle statement at all — which is the most plausible undocumented route by which a privileged account could destroy backups during their retention period, and precisely what this requirement asks about. Reachable only for self-produced off-platform dumps under S3 Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode, which binds every principal including the account root.

Essential Eight RAP-02 and RAP-03 require privileged access to be disabled after 12 months unless revalidated and after 45 days of inactivity. Neither exists: role_rank membership is a standing grant with no expiry and no inactivity sweep, so a grant made once holds forever. Both windows are ASD's own verbatim numbers and are the only ones that may be encoded.

Essential Eight RAP-13 requires just-in-time administration for administering systems and applications. Nothing in this tree elevates temporarily: role_rank is a standing grant and no admin session carries an expiry. Discharge is a time-bounded elevation whose expiry the RLS admin predicate actually consults, so an expired session stops satisfying it rather than merely being marked expired.

Essential Eight PA-01 and POS-01 require an automated method of asset discovery at least fortnightly to support vulnerability scanning. The lockfile is already a deterministic dependency inventory but nothing emits it AS an inventory artefact. pnpm 11 ships `pnpm sbom` natively and design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md section 8 already records SBOM CONSUMPTION — diffing against the previous release tag and redding on an unallowlisted addition — as the differentiating control, deferred undated. This row dates it.

Essential Eight PA-03 requires a vulnerability scanner at least DAILY for online services, and the shipped osv-scan schedule is WEEKLY. Found by grading rather than assumed, and the diff-aware PR lane does not close it: osv-scan.yml's own header records that a tree shipping a vulnerable pin from before the advisory never reds on the diff-aware half. Discharge is a daily cadence for the internet-facing class, or a reviewed regrade if the class is argued narrower.

Essential Eight PA-11 (online services), PA-13 (applications) and POS-16 (operating systems) require products no longer supported by vendors to be removed or replaced. 0.9.9 DISCHARGED PA-13 and disproved the plan’s assumption that one artefact would cover all three. The built closure reads the npm registry’s own `deprecated` flags out of the RESOLVED pnpm-lock.yaml (a committed third-party artefact, so the check is hermetic), dispositions every one of them in the reviewed tools/eol.json, and RECOMPUTES each row’s production-vs-development scope from the lockfile instead of believing it — which on its first run disproved the note about to be written, since five of the scaffold’s six deprecated packages are development-only and uuid@7 is not (it arrives through expo -> @expo/config-plugins -> xcode). WHAT IS STILL OWED IS THE OTHER TWO ROWS, and neither is a scheduling matter. PA-11 wants ONLINE SERVICES: Supabase, Vercel, GitHub Actions, the npm registry, EAS. None of them has a support flag in any artefact this tree contains, and asking their APIs is refused by the hermeticity rule in CONTRIBUTING. POS-16 wants PLATFORMS: the CI runner image, the Node major, the Postgres major, the mobile target SDKs. store-policy.json holds currency floors, which assert recency and not vendor support, and POS-15 already claims framework-floor.json plus the version-sync step as its runtime-currency alternate control — so grading POS-16 on the same artefact would double-count one control across two requirements. Discharge for both is a reviewed per-service and per-platform support register with its own freshness window, or an honest permanent ceiling; it is a decision about where the boundary sits, not a build to schedule.

Essential Eight PA-06, PA-07 and PA-10 carry ASD's verbatim 48-hour, two-week and one-month windows for applying vendor mitigations, and no control measures advisory-publication against deployment time. framework-floor.json is clockless and offline by design: it holds a version floor, not a window. Discharge must encode ONLY ASD's stated numbers — the assessment guidance sets no window for 'in a timely manner', and inventing a 24- or 72-hour SLA would manufacture a contractual obligation with no framework backing.

The standing ask-the-CLI config census is blocked UPSTREAM, not on scheduling: no Supabase CLI subcommand at the 2.113.0 pin parses config.toml without side effects (config push needs a project ref, functions list needs a token, status binds to whichever stack holds the default ports and prints SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET). The consumer deferral entry carries the full re-check record and the standing per-arrival rule; this row is its census twin — it discharges only when the side-effect-free subcommand actually ships, by deleting both together.

The committed-lockfile floor 0.9.0 opened inside version-sync (the absent-lockfile NOTE it replaces claimed 'CI always has one', which was false: the shipped workflows run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which hard-fails without a committed lockfile, and a fresh resolution drifts against the live registry) falls due at 0.10.0. The 0.10.0 migrations record owes this expiry the way every record has paid its predecessor's.

The commit-time installed-not-dormant floor 0.9.0 opened inside wiring (a committed lefthook.yml with nothing in .git/hooks is layer 2 disarmed while every description of the harness counts it armed) falls due at 0.10.0. The 0.10.0 migrations record owes this expiry alongside the version-sync lockfile floor's.

The env-through-register rule (0.9.5) is harness-OWNED, so `update` arms it on every install at once, while the two sites it was written for are SEEDED — an upgrading consumer would meet a hard-red lint step on files `update` cannot rewrite and they never touched. A lint rule cannot carry a rampNote, so the two paths sit in the rule's `ignores` as its ramp, paired with a 0.9.5 seededSourceFixes instruction that `doctor` surfaces. 0.10.0 owes the removal of those two ignore lines, once the source fix has had a release to land. Found by upgrade-lane leg I, not by review.

The agent-surface truth checks 0.9.5 opened inside docs-sync (the AGENTS.md line-budget claims-check and the body command closure over .claude/{rules,commands,skills,agents}) fall due at 0.10.0. Ramped because AGENTS.md is seeded — every pre-0.9.5 install keeps the old ~200 sentence update cannot rewrite — and skills may be consumer-authored. The 0.10.0 migrations record owes this expiry.

The ADR content-shape check 0.9.5 opened inside docs-sync (load-bearing sections with real bodies, closed-vocabulary Status, resolvable corpus refs, allowlisted source hosts) falls due at 0.11.0 — two releases, because consumer-authored ADRs are exactly the content ramps exist for and a documentation debt cannot rot the tree meanwhile. The 0.11.0 migrations record owes this expiry.

The vertical-anatomy + intra-vertical layering laws 0.9.5 opened inside boundaries (dual barrels, pure barrels, domain purity, DAL-through-the-port, events purity, the select('*') ban — the worked notes anatomy as law, lib/vertical-anatomy.mjs) fall due at 0.10.0. The 0.10.0 migrations record owes this expiry; pre-0.9.5 installs see NOTEs until then.

0.9.9 added the MFA rail and with it ten reviewed [auth.mfa] keys across four new config sections. tools/auth-posture.json is harness-OWNED so `update` arms the new posture on every install at once, while supabase/config.toml is SEEDED so `update` cannot write the section the posture now demands — the exact ambush upgrade-lane leg I caught for the 0.9.5 env register, and the reason this ramp is scoped to the [auth.mfa] findings alone rather than to the whole gate (the redirect-allowlist and session-cookie findings have nothing to do with this release and stay hard). Falls due at 0.10.0: the seededSourceFixes channel parks the instruction in .harness/pending/ meanwhile, and rampNote reds the finding itself once the deadline arrives. The 0.10.0 migrations record owes this expiry the way every record has paid its predecessor's.

0.9.9 added the end-of-life census to `version-sync`, and its subject is tools/eol.json — a NEW SEEDED file, DELIBERATELY PLANTED rather than withheld. Withholding it was the obvious move and the wrong one: the ramp would expire at 0.10.0 into a hard red demanding a file `update` had refused to give the install. Planting it creates the opposite problem, and this ramp is what pays for it: a consumer's lockfile is a SUPERSET of the harness's, so the six planted rows will not cover every deprecated package their tree resolves, and may name one it no longer resolves — both directions red on a tree whose code did not change. That is the same upgrade ambush the [auth.mfa] posture ramp exists for, and it takes the same shape. THE RAMP COVERS EVERY FINDING THE SECTION PRODUCES, from ONE call site, scoped to that section alone so the rest of `version-sync` stays hard: an upgrading consumer gets a dated list of exactly what to disposition instead of a wall of reds, and a fresh 0.9.9 scaffold never sees the ramp at all because its baseVersion is already 0.9.9. Falls due at 0.10.0, which the 0.10.0 migrations record owes the way every record has paid its predecessor's.

The suppressions census (inline-disable/escape-comment accounting) ships as a NEW chain step, and a new step is PRICED, not free — the full injection inventory, in order: a configSteps record anchored on a 0.1.x-vintage step every consumer chain carries, the chain-budget row FIRST (a step with no row reds the budget closure), the injections.json canary, the enforcement-tiers row, the validate.floor.json regen, the AGENTS.md gate-list escape re-opened at minVersion 0.10.0 (the injected step grows every existing chain while the seeded AGENTS.md still documents 34), the check-docs-sync test fixture move, the upgrade lane's leg-A doctrine flip, and the chain-budget re-record at 36/36 before ANY published figure — a 34-step measurement stops licensing prose the moment the chain reaches 36.

The resilience closure (retry/timeout/backoff posture over the seams that call out) ships as the second NEW chain step of 0.10.0 and pays the SAME priced injection inventory as suppressions-chain-step — one inventory, two steps, and the chain-budget re-record at 36/36 happens once, after both land, before any published figure.

The cross-platform validate legs (macOS/Windows) run schedule-gated as measurement lanes, so off-Linux validate is proven nightly rather than per-commit — the README's platform-honesty qualifier states exactly that. After their first green scheduled runs, 0.10.0 owes the promotion of the schedule-gated static lane into the per-PR/tag population, at which point the qualifier is deleted rather than carried.

A torn or half-written .claude/hooks file fails OPEN by Claude Code's exit-code contract — probed empirically 2026-08-10 during the installer atomic-write work: a hook that cannot parse exits non-blocking, so the guard it carried simply is not there. 0.9.0 contains the write side (tmp+rename, snapshots, --rollback); the residual is a LAUNCHER that fails closed when the file it wraps is torn. Condition, not a date: the discharge shape depends on the hook-invocation contract, re-probed at every Claude Code pin bump.

The enterprise-facing controls crosswalk + threat model is GENERATABLE — harness.config.mjs (the chain), the guard-rules tables (the hooks), and tests/canary/injections.json (the proofs) are the three machine-read inputs — but it is gated on the licensing/wholeness decision design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md records for the conformance map: built whole against Annex I directly, or not at all, because a claimed level with an unmapped requirement is worse than no claim.

SECURITY.md ships the coordinated-disclosure channel but names no response SLA. Condition: the SLA is a maintainer-capacity commitment nobody should date on someone else's behalf — it discharges when the maintainer writes the sentence, by deleting this row with that sentence as evidence. (The row's former SCA half was paid at 0.9.5: hygiene.yml#factory-sca, the scheduled OSV lane over the factory's own lockfile.)

The differentiating control was never PRODUCING an SBOM (pnpm 11 does that natively) — it is CONSUMING one: diffing against the previous release tag and redding on an added component that is not allowlisted. design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md §8 records it deliberately undated; it becomes ACTIONABLE when the version-sync committed-lockfile ramp expires at 0.10.0, because a lockfile every install must commit is the input the diff needs.

DSR erase EXISTS — session.deleteAccount plus the delete-account Edge Function, and the expo-policy gate requires the account-deletion surface on any auth-bearing app (Apple 5.1.1(v)) — but only the mobile surface reaches it, and tools/data-flow.json declares no erase.surface record, so the gate that holds export to its target has nothing to hold erase to. 0.10.0 owes the WEB erase surface and the data-flow record; the README's honest-losses sentence names this row.

The accessibility-reviewer claims a WCAG 2.2 AA audit while the axe e2e sweeps run withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa']) — the 2.0/2.1-era tag set, which never selects the 2.2-only rules — so the machine half of the claim checks less than the prose asserts. 0.10.0 owes the tag widening (wcag21aa/wcag22aa) or the honest narrowing of the reviewer's claim, whichever review decides.

sites.mustContain: What this deliberately does NOT solve

obligations.reason: The 0.9.5 e2ee rails DECLARE three ports with no implementations — RecipientWrapPort (org sharing: an org-mate's RLS-visible row is ciphertext they cannot open), RecoveryPort (a lost device is lost data; WebCrypto ships no Argon2 and PBKDF2-as-the-KDF would be a dishonest default), and DeviceSyncPort (a second device has no path to the root key). Condition, not a dated row: each needs a design decision the harness should not date on a consumer's behalf, and the honest state is a declaration plus a stated loss rather than a promise. This row anchors the declarations to the README section that states their cost, so an implementation cannot quietly turn a declared port into a claim without the register moving too. Also open by construction: the web KeystoreAdapter returns raw bytes, which forecloses a non-extractable CryptoKey handle, and the keyring exports no rewrap primitive so key rotation is a full client-side re-encryption pass.

The DAL laws (port-presence, dal-client-value-import) and events-purity are keyed on DIRECTORY NAMES — src/data/, src/events.ts — so a vertical that names its data layer src/repo/ satisfies them by construction: an adversarial review put a module-scope createClient with a service-role key in packages/verticals/sneaky/src/repo/ and the scan reported zero findings. The laws that read a WHOLE tree (domain purity is scoped the same way; select-star and the barrels are not) are the ones with teeth. Condition rather than dated: closing it means either mandating the anatomy by name (the directory-shaped proxy metric this gate's own header rejects) or deriving the data layer from the port's import graph, which is a design decision. The architecture-reviewer's trigger covers packages/*/src/** whatever the folder is called, which is the compensating control today.

crypto-primitives-one-door matches a `crypto.subtle` member chain and NAMED cipher imports, and an adversarial review showed it misses the namespace routes: `import { webcrypto } from 'node:crypto'` then webcrypto.subtle.*, a default or `* as` import used as nodeCrypto.createCipheriv(...), and `const c = require('node:crypto')` followed by c.createCipheriv(...). Each needs binding-level tracking (which local names alias the module) rather than the single-node test the rule does now, and a half-tracked version would red honest code. The compensating controls are the mobile cipher-library one-door, the weak-crypto-algorithm write-guard, and the security reviewers on the crypto trigger paths.

A census entry's `module` value is validated as a non-empty string and never against the real module set, so a typo'd module name parks the stale arm PERMANENTLY dormant while the entry still pre-authorises a ./client barrel and a mobile runtime dependency — the silent widening the stale arm exists to prevent. The module list is canonical and readable (installer/lib/layout.mjs MODULES, template/modules/*), but the gate ships to consumers where neither path is guaranteed present, so the check needs a shipped list rather than a factory import. Condition until that list has a home.

The architecture-reviewer's trigger (0.9.5) is scoped to packages/** plus the two structural registers, deliberately NOT apps/** — the triggers file's own doctrine is narrowness first, because an over-matching trigger makes every diff owe every reviewer and gets routed around. Condition: widen to apps/*/lib/** (the web seam files) only once a release of reviewer-ledger evidence shows the packages-scoped trigger earns its verdicts rather than producing noise; the evidence is the .harness/reviewer-ledger.jsonl population at the widening review.

The full Stop chain executes off-Linux nowhere: the blocker is the DATABASE, not the shell — rls-isolation needs the live Supabase stack (Docker), which the Windows/macOS runners do not carry, while the gate/hook LOGIC is already proven cross-platform by the Windows unit matrix. Condition: discharge needs a supported off-Linux local-stack story upstream, re-checked at every Supabase CLI pin bump, not a date this repo can set.

tools/store-policy.json holds a harness FLOOR the harness must be able to ship (iosToolchain's Xcode floor, androidTargetSdk — check-version-sync reds when iosToolchain is missing and tells the consumer to run `update` to restore it) and a consumer TUNABLE in the same file (iosEncryption.nonExemptAllowed + reason, which check-expo-policy's own failure text tells the consumer to set). Owned, it is hash-pinned, so the demanded edit reads as tampering; seeded, `update` can no longer deliver the floor — 0.9.5 tried the seeded flip and upgrade-lane leg E caught it immediately, a v0.3.0 install keeping its pre-0.7.0 file and redding BOTH version-sync and docs-sync. Neither classification is right because the file is two files. Same shape and same remedy as auth-posture-consumer-tunable-split below: floor rows owned and pinned, tunable rows seeded with declared bounds. Condition, not dated: the split is a design decision, and the wrong half-fix is worse than the honest record.

tools/auth-posture.json holds the harness FLOOR and the consumer-TUNABLE values in one reviewed file, so a consumer legitimately retuning a tunable produces the same diff shape as weakening the floor, and review carries the whole burden of telling them apart. 0.10.0 owes the split: floor rows owned and pinned, tunable rows seeded with declared bounds.

The mutation critical-surface definition (tools/lib/mutation-critical.mjs, shared by the PR diff-scoper and the nightly) is harness-OWNED while every file it names is SEEDED — a consumer whose tree diverges from the exemplar paths silently mutates less than the lane claims. Condition: the discharge shape (derive the surface from the consumer's own inventories vs seed the definition) is an open design decision the ratchet's set semantics depend on.

At the OUTAGE rung fail-open is a pure window: withFailOpen lets every request through while the backend is down, and the README records that loss. The memory limiter already exists in the package but is wired only at the CONFIGURATION rung (no Upstash credentials at boot) — 0.10.0 owes wiring it as the outage fallback too, so a backend outage degrades to per-instance limiting instead of none.

Supabase Data API grants stop being automatic for projects created on or after this date (three roles including service_role, SEQUENCES revoked too, failure is SQLSTATE 42501 not a silent 404, and the auto_expose_new_tables restore flag is removed the SAME day). The closure SHIPPED in 0.6.0 inside schema-rls; this row is the dated re-verification that the shipped closure and its prose still describe the regime as it actually lands.

Google Play's target API deadline (36 general, 35 Wear/Automotive, 34 TV/XR; two requirement families — submission and continued-distribution). CRA Article 14 reporting applies from this date (Art. 71(2); a SINGLE reporting end-point simultaneously accessible to ENISA, not three recipients).
